next_step: Closed-lost. Set cadence to re-engage Q3 2026; deliver post-mortem and structured-output playbook.
notes:
Background: Mosaic Contracts Labs is a mid-to-large legaltech vendor building automated clause extraction and executive summaries for enterprise legal teams. They ran a 6-week POC with Redwood hosted API (jan-feb 2026). Incumbent: Nimbus AI Platform (already in procurement at several of their anchor customers).

Timeline (short):
- 2025-09-01: Initial intro (AE Sofia). Demo scheduled; interested in on-prem options for EU customers.
- 2026-01-05: POC kickoff (SE Rajiv). Data sync to VPC staging.
- 2026-01-20: First evaluation: Redwood matched latency SLAs but produced inconsistent JSON schema for "extracted_clauses" endpoint. Team flagged missing required fields.
- 2026-01-27: Engineering deep-dive. Found tool-calling failures when pipeline invoked 3rd-party clause-normalizer. Root cause: function-call tokenization differences and inconsistent field ordering after model upgrade. Jira INF-4021 opened.
- 2026-02-03: Mosaic engineering ran A/B vs incumbent. Nimbus returned deterministic, schema-valid output >95% of time; Redwood POC ~78% with regressions after model refresh (noted 2026-01-30).
- 2026-02-12: Security review flagged audit / KMS gaps for private deployment and asked for SOC2 attestation + HSM integration (ticket SEC-1183).
- 2026-02-18: Final sync. Mosaic product lead said "we can't ship if we need to hand-fix outputs — structured JSON is non-negotiable." Decision: move to Nimbus for initial rollout.

POC Findings (engineer notes):
- Strengths: good latency, attractive cost-per-token for long sequences, SDK simple.
- Failure modes: inconsistent function/tool-calling semantics; occasional top-level hallucinations that break downstream parser; output occasionally missing required keys (e.g., "obligations.amount") leading to exceptions in normalization pipeline.
- Repro: failures spiked after Redwood model profile update on 2026-01-30 (regression vs earlier snapshot).

Customer quotes / signals:
- "We need deterministic structured output; human-in-the-loop isn't in the roadmap." — Product lead (M. Alvarez)
- Internal champion (Dir of ML Ops) left the company mid-POC; momentum declined.

Commercials / procurement:
- Expected ARR 150k-300k for enterprise pack + private deployment.
- Budget freeze at Q1 exec review due to procurement choosing incumbent and legal risk tolerance.

Why lost / current state:
- Primary loss reason: quality regression vs incumbent on structured outputs and tool-calling reliability.
- Secondary: security integration timeline (HSM / audit) estimated 8+ weeks vs incumbent already validated.
- Tertiary: internal champion left during evaluation; no executive sponsor to push remediation.
- Status: closed-lost to Nimbus; relationship cordial. They asked for a short write-up of issues and a potential remediation timeline.

Next steps for Redwood (recommended):
- Deliver concise POC post-mortem (1 pager) with timeline to fix deterministic JSON + tool-calling fidelity. Attach to Drive (mosaic-poc-postmortem.pdf).
- Offer a limited re-run with pinned model snapshot (no auto-updates) + contractually guaranteed schema stability for a short trial.
- Track quarterly for re-engage; target Q3 2026 after their initial rollout with incumbent.
- Coordinate security team to produce SOC2 + HSM integration brief; share templates for audit.

Notes on messaging: keep it technical and pragmatic. Emphasize deterministic generation (schema validation hooks, strict function-calling semantics), exportable audit logs, and escalation path for regressions. Avoid blaming model changes; show root-cause + patch plan.

Attachments / artifacts: POC results CSV, sample failed JSONs, link to Fireflies call ff-2026-02-10-4492 transcript.

CRM shorthand: closed-lost -> Nimbus. champion_left -> yes. security_blocker -> SOC2 + KMS. budget -> freeze. follow_up -> Q3-2026.
